correctness.rationale: The positive-semidefinite Hermitian Gram representation is necessary and sufficient in ambient complex dimension at least three. Its determinant gives exact feasible c, the endpoint eigenvalues give sharp formulas, and the derivative of the cubic power sum equals 2pt^3 times a second divided difference. Hermite–Genocchi makes the sign exactly sign((p-1)(p-2)) for positive interior eigenvalues. Continuity handles rank-deficient endpoints, the largest-root derivative handles p=∞, and traces handle p=1,2. Reproducible finite checks support but do not replace these analytic arguments.

originality.rationale: The sharp all-exponent two-sided feasible Schatten envelope and its unique phase extremizers are not an implication-equivalent statement of the inspected Carbery general upper inequality or of Bargmann Gram reconstruction. The proof adds a strict divided-difference phase-order theorem, the overlap 1/2 rank-change boundary, and the reversal for 1<p<2 versus p>2. Closest publicly indexed qutrit off-diagonal-moment work has a different constrained operator; full-text access to that record was unavailable, and broader classical spectral moment theory remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A broad older theorem on power sums of three nonnegative roots at fixed first two elementary symmetric functions could imply the monotonicity step; this would limit independent priority.
The qutrit phase-holonomy record was only available as an indexed summary, not full text, although its stated operator and constraints differ.
No independent literature-priority certification or external expert review has taken place.

value.rationale: This is the minimal three-state configuration in which fixed pairwise orthogonality coefficients conceal a gauge-invariant phase. The theorem determines the entire exact Schatten range for each overlap and all positive real exponents, the strict reversal at p=2, and a sharp geometric transition at overlap 1/2. It is a motivated complete natural classification, not merely a reparameterized known upper inequality or an arbitrary finite table.
